descriptions.text: Steam Engineer's Key. Allows access to Iron Tangle employee-only areas and actions on all 400 steam-type trains of the Tangle.

beats.headline: A plate that wants a key
beats.text: Aboard a red line subway car, with monsters in the next one, Carl gets down on his knees and pulls up the panel in the gangway floor, hoping to find the train's electrical system and the controls for the couplers. Under it is a small metal door with a lock, like a breaker box. He puts his hand on it and gets an error: the service plate is magically locked, and he needs a Red Line Engineer's Key. Do you have a key? No you don't. So back off. Carl puts the panel back. It will have to be the nuclear option.

beats.headline: Colour coded
beats.text: From what Gore-Gore has let slip, Katia reckons they can get back to the start if they can get into an engine car. They need an engineer's key, she says; he probably has it in his inventory, and with it they could break into the first car while the train is still moving. Carl agrees, but the keys are colour coded, so an ochre key will only work on ochre trains, and crashing a train to get one stops the rest of the line, which would make the key useless. Doesn't a crash only stop the trains behind it, asks Donut? Take the key and jump ahead on the Nightmare Express or one of the other fast loop trains. That's brilliant, says Carl.

beats.headline: Off the third rail
beats.text: One clockwork Mongo explodes when it touches metal on the third rail; the other drags Gore-Gore's corpse up against the wall of the channel, and Carl loots it: 498 gold and three items. An Ochre Line Engineer's Key, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, and the neighborhood map. The map is the surprise. It fills his interface not with the area around him but with the whole ochre line, every stop from station 11 to 435, and where every train on it is right now.

beats.headline: Bronze, in the gore
beats.text: Carl is in the Nightmare Express's cab and has just boxed up its bricks. In the mess of gore, where the driver or the war mage was pushed against the box at the back, he finds a small satchel holding 350 gold and a large, bronze key: a Steam Engineer's Key. It allows access to the Tangle's employee-only areas and actions on all four hundred of its steam-type trains. Only then does he relax enough to look around. He is alive, and he has stolen a goddamned train.

beats.headline: Three keys in the list
beats.text: At Abyss Station, Carl reads a portal over the pit. It is gated by conveyance type and to key holders: a crawler must be on a gated conveyance, or have a key equipped or held outside inventory, and compatible keys have been marked. Sorting his inventory on the way back down the stairs, he finds three: the Ochre Key, the Steam Train Key, and the souvenir hat from the start of the floor. His message to every crawler on his chat list sets out the ways through, and one of them is to kill an engineer and take his key, without crashing the train.

beats.headline: The Vermillion key
beats.text: Hekla is dead, Donut has her corpse up and lurching at the Daughters, and Carl is tugging at its crossbow when he sees the square access panel in the gangway floor. Katia has to get the Vermillion key from Hekla's corpse, he tells her, and it has to be her, because she killed Hekla. Get the key first. The engine doors were blocked so they never locked, but uncoupling the car still needs it. Once the cab door is slid shut and locked against the Daughters' spells, he asks whether she got it. I got it, says Katia. Not that it matters now.

beats.headline: In Donut's mouth
beats.text: The last of the hat-wearing crawlers have gone through the portal to yard H, and the party follows on the cart. Carl puts his own hat on. Donut does not want to remove her tiara, so instead she sighs and holds an engineer's key in her mouth, and Mongo goes into his carrier. Carl suspects that since the cart itself is allowed through, they need neither hat nor key, but there is a cliff on the other side and no sense risking it. He eases the cart through, and just like that, it is done.
